title: Completion of a flat module with projective reduction is flat Mittag-Leffler
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal, and assume $R$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $P$ be any flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] such that $P/IP$ is projective over $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Put $P^\wedge=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}P/I^nP$, the $R$-module of families $x_n\in P/I^nP$ compatible under the quotient maps, with componentwise operations; $I^nP$ is the submodule generated by $ap$ with $a\in I^n$ and $p\in P$. Then $P^\wedge$ is flat over $R$ and is a Mittag-Leffler $R$-module [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module].

proof.text: Put $F=\bigoplus_{p\in P}R$, explicitly the module of finitely supported families of coefficients indexed by the underlying set of $P$. Define $v:F\to P$ by $v((r_p)_p)=\sum_p r_pp$. This is $R$-linear and surjective since the family with coefficient $1$ at $p$ and zero elsewhere maps to $p$. Set $K=\ker(v)$ and let $u:K\to F$ be inclusion. Thus $u$ is injective and $\operatorname{im}(u)=\ker(v)$, giving $0\to K\to F\to P\to0$.

source.place: Tag 05DK, lemma-lift-ML, proof: first sentence, choosing the free cover; explicit construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-projective-reduction-completion-splitting] with $E=F$ and $M=P$ to the sequence just constructed. Its two extra hypotheses are exactly the assumed flatness of $P$ and projectivity of $P/IP$ over $R/I$. Consequently the quotient-level map $r=\widehat v:\widehat F\to P^\wedge$ has an $R$-linear section $s:P^\wedge\to\widehat F$ with $r\circ s=\mathrm{id}_{P^\wedge}$. In particular, $s$ is injective and, after tensoring with any module $Q$, $\mathrm{id}_Q\otimes s$ is still split injective: its left inverse is $\mathrm{id}_Q\otimes r$. The analogous assertion holds for $s\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q$, by the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 05DK, lemma-lift-ML, proof: second sentence, splitting the completed sequence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-completed-free-flat-mittag-leffler] to the set underlying $P$. The ring $R$ is Noetherian and $I$-adically complete by hypothesis, and its module $F$ is precisely the finitely supported family module in that statement. It follows that $\widehat F$ is flat over $R$ and Mittag-Leffler. No finite generation of $P$ or of the indexing set is assumed.

source.place: Tag 05DK, lemma-lift-ML, proof: last sentence, the completed-free-module case.

proof.text: For any injective $R$-linear map $f:Q_1\to Q_2$, let $z\in Q_1\otimes_R P^\wedge$ satisfy $(f\otimes\mathrm{id})z=0$. Naturality of the tensor maps gives $(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\widehat F})(\mathrm{id}_{Q_1}\otimes s)z=(\mathrm{id}_{Q_2}\otimes s)(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{P^\wedge})z=0$. Since $\widehat F$ is flat, $(\mathrm{id}_{Q_1}\otimes s)z=0$; applying $\mathrm{id}_{Q_1}\otimes r$ gives $z=0$. Thus tensoring $f$ with $P^\wedge$ is injective, which is exactly flatness by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The naturality identity is verified on $q\otimes p$ and hence on all tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 05DK, lemma-lift-ML, proof: third sentence, direct-summand inheritance of flatness, written from the definition.

proof.text: Fix any set $J$ and family $(Q_j)_{j\in J}$, and use the canonical maps $\theta$ of [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module]. If $z\in P^\wedge\otimes_R\prod_jQ_j$ satisfies $\theta_{P^\wedge,(Q_j)}(z)=0$, then $\theta_{\widehat F,(Q_j)}((s\otimes\mathrm{id})z)=(\prod_j(s\otimes\mathrm{id}_{Q_j}))\theta_{P^\wedge,(Q_j)}(z)=0$. This identity holds on $p\otimes(q_j)_j$ since both sides have $j$-coordinate $s(p)\otimes q_j$, and extends by linearity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The Mittag-Leffler property of $\widehat F$ makes its $\theta$ injective, so $(s\otimes\mathrm{id})z=0$. Applying $r\otimes\mathrm{id}$ gives $z=0$, as $rs=\mathrm{id}$. This proves the required Mittag-Leffler condition for $P^\wedge$, including empty $J$.
